semantic_adjudication.reason: The candidate asserts that the root initial entry should be unconditional. However, the supplied NL requirement quote is 'when power on, the system turn into human driving mode,' which explicitly makes the transition to HumanDriving conditional on the Power_On event. The model implements exactly this: transition:line:20 is [*] -> HumanDriving triggered by Power_On. The source trace tr_0001 confirms this is the authored transition. The inspection diagnostic INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL correctly identifies that the edge carries a trigger, but this is precisely what the NL requires—the NL says 'when power on,' not 'by default' or 'immediately.' The event consumer fact for Power_On showing reachable_consumer_transition_refs is empty is a consequence of the conditional initial edge, but the NL does not require Power_On to be consumable from a reachable state because the system is not yet in any operating state before Power_On. The supplied NL fact positively supports the model's design choice, defeating the alleged violation that an unconditional entry was required.

The model's transition:line:20 ([*] -> HumanDriving : Power_On) implements exactly this conditional entry. The NL does not require an unconditional default; it requires that Power_On triggers the transition to HumanDriving, which is precisely what the model provides.

decisions.basis: Dossier 0030:r3:i0: NL4.2 requirement quote, closed_model_inventory.states showing Autonomous children (Navigating, Parking only), exact_source_inventory.states confirming same two children, contract derivation requiring containment of 'auto final'.
decisions.reason: The complete closed-model inventory for Autonomous's children shows exactly two states: Navigating (line 11) and Parking (line 12). No state named 'auto final' or semantically equivalent exists. The contract derivation requires a distinct state with that name. However, the NL parenthetical '(auto final)' is a location qualifier that is genuinely ambiguous: it could be a literal state name (supporting the containment obligation) or a descriptive label for the Autonomous composite's terminal sub-state scope (in which case Navigating and Parking, being the actual leaf states from which the exit transitions originate, fulfill the role). Both readings are compatible with the supplied source and model facts. The source itself contains no state named 'auto final', which supports the descriptive-label reading. No explicit NL terminal clause or formal terminal edge binds 'auto final' to a specific model element, so the ambiguity survives.
decisions.violated_obligation: A state named 'auto final' must exist as a child of the composite Autonomous per the NL4.2 parenthetical location qualifier 'in (auto final)'.

decisions.basis: Dossier 0030:r3:i1: NL4.2 requirement quote, closed_model_inventory.transitions (all 9 checked, none from 'auto final'), state:HumanDriving:line:9 confirmed as target, working_contract macro tr_0006 segments (lines 16, 17, 19) showing existing Navigating/Parking to HumanDriving paths.
decisions.reason: The complete closed-model transition inventory (9 transitions) contains no edge originating from a state named 'auto final'. Since no such state exists (confirmed by the inventory), no transition can originate from it. The contract requires this specific transition endpoint. However, if '(auto final)' is a descriptive label for the Autonomous scope rather than a distinct state, then the existing transitions from Navigating (line 16) and Parking (line 17) to HumanDriving, which carry the Human_Steering_Cmd_Brake_Pressed event, collectively realize the intended behavioral effect of exiting Autonomous to HumanDriving on those triggers. decisions.violated_obligation: A transition must exist from the 'auto final' sub-state within Autonomous to HumanDriving, triggered by human steering command or brake pressed.

decisions.basis: Dossier 0030:r3:i2: NL5 requirement quote, inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers[Power_Off] showing single consumer, reachable_state_refs confirming 5 reachable states, exact_source_inventory.transitions confirming tr_0007 as sole Power Off transition, contract system-level scope assignment.
decisions.reason: The deterministic event_consumer_fact for Power_Off shows exactly one consumer transition (transition:line:22 from state:HumanDriving:line:9). Three other reachable operating states (Autonomous, Navigating, Parking) have no Power_Off consumer. The source inventory confirms tr_0007 is the only Power Off transition, originating solely from HumanDriving. The narrower reading (that the obligation applies only to HumanDriving, the state from which the author drew the transition) is a competent alternative initially, but is defeated by the explicit system-level scope assignment in the contract derivation. The contract's system-level scope is a supplied fact that excludes the narrower interpretation.
decisions.violated_obligation: The Power_Off event must be consumable from all reachable operating states (HumanDriving, Autonomous, Navigating, Parking) enabling transition to the final state, per the NL5 system-level scope.

decisions.basis: Dossier 0030:r3:i3: NL3 requirement quote 'when power on, the system turn into human driving mode', source line 2 showing [*] -> HumanDriving : Power On, FCSTM transition:line:20 with triggers=[Power_On], verify fact initial-entry status=refuted, event_consumer_fact for Power_On showing empty reachable consumers.
decisions.reason: The NL3 states 'when power on, the system turn into human driving mode.' This explicitly describes Power_On as the condition under which the system enters HumanDriving mode. The source implements exactly this: the initial edge (transition:line:20) carries Power_On as its trigger. The contract's expectation of an 'unconditional initial entry' contradicts the NL's own description, which makes Power_On the entry condition. The NL does not say 'the system is always in human driving mode' or 'the system starts in human driving mode by default'; it says the system TURNS INTO human driving mode WHEN power on. This conditional language supports the author's design of a Power_On-triggered entry. The UML formal invariant (initial edges must be unconditional) conflicts with the NL's design description, but the NL is the primary obligation source and its text supports the implementation. The rebutting reading (that the conditional entry is the correct design per the NL) survives because the NL explicitly describes Power_On as the trigger.
decisions.violated_obligation: The system root must have an unconditional initial entry into HumanDrivingMode so that the system begins in that operating state by default.

decisions.basis: Dossier 0030:r3:i7: NL2 requirement quote 'The autonomous mode has sub-states and is represented by a sub machine state' (plural), source lines 8-9 showing Navigating and Parking as Autonomous children, contract cardinality_binding_id=CARD-BIND-NL2-CARD-1 with required=1 actual=2.

The reachable operating states Autonomous (state:Autonomous:line:10), Navigating (state:Navigating:line:11), and Parking (state:Parking:line:12) have no Power_Off consumer transition. The source inventory confirms tr_0007 is the only Power Off transition, originating solely from HumanDriving.
issues.reason: The derived contract REF-011 requires system-wide Power_Off coverage. The deterministic event_consumer_fact closes with exactly one reachable consumer (HumanDriving). Three other reachable operating states (Autonomous, Navigating, Parking) lack any Power_Off transition. The source inventory confirms the same gap: only tr_0007 carries Power Off, from HumanDriving alone. This is a precise coverage deficit, not an ambiguous binding.
issues.requirement_quote: when power off, it will transit to final state
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The NL phrase 'it will transit to final state' uses the pronoun 'it' without explicitly enumerating all states. One could argue the obligation is only for the state from which the author drew the transition (HumanDriving), and that UML composite exit semantics might implicitly allow a top-level final transition to apply to nested states. However, the FCSTM does not implement such implicit propagation: Navigating and Parking have no Power_Off handler.
issues.title: Power_Off event not consumable from all reachable operating states

issues.expected: The system root must have an unconditional initial entry into HumanDrivingMode so that the system begins in that operating state by default.
issues.observed: The only root-level initial edge (transition:line:20: [*] -> HumanDriving) carries a Power_On trigger, making it conditional. The inspection diagnostic INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL and verify fact initial-entry:transition:line:20 (refuted, has_trigger=true) confirm this. The event consumer fact for Power_On shows reachable_consumer_transition_refs is empty, meaning no reachable state can consume Power_On. The reference inspection fact W_INITIAL_UNCONDITIONAL_MISSING confirms the root composite lacks an unconditional fallback entry.
issues.reason: The behavior_consequence lens identifies that the conditional initial entry has a direct operational consequence: the system cannot begin operation because the only path from the initial pseudostate requires an event (Power_On) that has no reachable consumer. This is a distinct behavioral failure from the structural observation that the edge carries a trigger.
issues.requirement_quote: when power on, the system turn into human driving mode
issues.strongest_rebuttal: One could argue that the Power_On-triggered initial edge IS the system's entry mechanism and that requiring Power_On before the system becomes active is semantically valid. However, in standard state machine semantics, an initial pseudostate edge must be unconditional to establish a default active state; a conditional initial edge creates a deadlock at startup where no state is active and no event can be consumed.
issues.title: Root initial entry is conditional on Power_On, leaving no unconditionally active default state
